model.rationale: Aderholt holds a seat with an R+33 lean, has been renominated, and out-raised his challenger by roughly 65-to-1, while markets give the Democrat about a 1% chance. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting movement, the forecast stays firmly in Safe R territory.

overview:
Northwest Alabama's 4th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+33. Robert Aderholt, a longtime incumbent, was renominated and enters the general election with a large financial edge: about $750,000 on hand compared with roughly $400 for Democratic nominee Amanda Pusczek, who has raised under $16,000. No outside groups are active in the race, and no public polls are available.

Prediction markets price Aderholt's chances at about 99%, and no expert raters list the contest as competitive. The forecast expects Aderholt to win comfortably, with the Democrat's main hope resting on an unforeseen shock rather than any visible campaign dynamic.
